_note: The claims model holds each load-bearing proposition the book asserts, plus the AUDIT PREDICATE (`contradicted_by`) naming what prose would negate it. JUDGMENT-AUDIT BOUNDARY (DESIGN §4.2): the contradiction check is a SEMANTIC judgment-audit owned by a review gate, NOT a blocking lint; only the structural / schema checks (C1–C6 + the C7-drift freshness check) are mechanical and may ever go blocking, and the watch-phrase surfacing lint (C7) stays AUDIT-ONLY FOREVER (a hit is a review candidate, never a verdict). REFLEXIVE PAYOFF (DESIGN §4.3): the two aides — the pre-edit consult (`catalog.py claims <chapter>`, the CONSTRAINT that aims the editing agent away from the drift) and the watch-phrase lint plus judgment-audit (the SENSOR that catches it after) — instantiate the book's own Alignment Thesis on its own manuscript. The model does not merely record the constraint/sensor distinction; it applies it to the book's prose.

claims.statement: MAGE is not a general theory of knowledge work; its broader claims apply where work is functionally engineering.
claims.contradicted_by: Prose extending MAGE to arbitrary knowledge work, or claiming a profession transfers wholesale rather than surface-by-surface where consequential outcomes are deliberately controlled through specialized knowledge, evidence, judgment, and accountable authority.
claims.anchor: NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT (expan-4 L373, recorded alongside the canonical statement): MAGE is not a general theory of knowledge work. Its broader claims apply where work is engineering in the book's functional sense: consequential outcomes are being deliberately controlled through specialized knowledge, evidence, judgment, and accountable authority. This pair governs Chapter 1, Chapter 6, section 7.3, the Conclusion, figures, glossary definitions, and future edits. ALSO governed here (expan-4 L310-317): the environment-vocabulary house rule — engineered/engineering environment descriptive; governed engineering environment the achieved property; Governed Engineering Environment (GEE) the construct; free-standing 'governed environment' avoided; NO domain-general governed-environment layer above GEE.

claims.statement: MAGE governs agentic engineering work; engineering is defined functionally, not institutionally.
claims.contradicted_by: Prose defining MAGE's framework-level scope without the engineering qualifier (governing 'consequential agentic work' or 'knowledge work' simpliciter), or bounding it institutionally by profession rather than by the functional definition (informed control + expertise + evidence + answerability).
claims.anchor: CANONICAL MODEL STATEMENT (expan-4 L369, the invariant this row governs): MAGE is a framework for governing agentic engineering work by engineering the environment through which agents act. Engineering is defined by the exercise of informed control over consequential systems under conditions of expertise and responsibility, not by membership in a conventionally named engineering discipline. Software engineering is MAGE's first worked domain and the source of the evidence in this book. Modeling makes consequential engineering knowledge and intent explicit. Alignment gives selected engineering obligations evidence and enforcement outside the producing reasoner. Governance conversion preserves useful judgment in durable engineering structure; when later work benefits from that structure, it becomes engineering capital. Together, these mechanisms create the Governed Engineering Environment. Implementation and mechanisms may increasingly be delegated. Engineering responsibility remains with an accountable human or institution. Stated in prose at: glossary Engineering entry; What This Book Argues opener; Preface 'consequential engineering work' paragraphs. GOVERNANCE HIERARCHY (expan-4 #8, author-ordered capture): Governance is the arrangements by which work and consequence are directed, bounded, evaluated, admitted, and escalated. Control is sufficient capacity and authority to intervene and remain responsible. Enforcement is the mechanisms that bind selected obligations. Alignment is the MAGE principle placing such enforcement outside the producing reasoner where adequate decision is possible. Do not purge 'control'; it names the human property that must be retained.

claims.statement: Engineering discipline must be mechanized, not remembered: push it into tooling so correctness never depends on recall.
claims.contradicted_by: Relying on an agent or human remembering, or being careful, as the enforcement.
claims.anchor: Preface premise (SE-at-Google touchstone): discipline is mechanized into tooling, not left to memory or care.

claims.statement: A model's value is both its structure and the invariants it lets you enforce.
distinguishes: the structure — records, edges, state machines — that names the parts and gives tools something to read
the checked invariants — the predicates a gate holds true, which complete the model's value rather than replace the schema
claims.contradicted_by: Prose that treats a model's schema ALONE as its whole value — counting an unchecked structure as a finished model — OR that dismisses the schema as worthless, denying that the structure carries value the invariants complete.
claims.anchor: 3.1 'The coherence triangle': the model provides two kinds of value — the schema names the parts, and the checked invariants (each earned from a failure) complete it; the invariants and gate complete the schema's value rather than replacing it.

claims.statement: A model is not a governance mechanism until something reads or enforces it.
claims.contradicted_by: Prose counting a bare model — read by nothing, enforced by nothing — as a governance mechanism.
claims.anchor: 3.3 'What counts as a mechanism': a structured model on disk aims nobody — the model supplies the policy; the mechanism that reads or enforces it supplies the holding.

claims.statement: Models are the language of engineering; software could not afford them until agents cut sync cost.
claims.contradicted_by: Framing models as a nice-to-have or a software-specific trick rather than engineering's common language.
claims.anchor: Preface universal-language touchstone + 6.0 'models as a common language of mature engineering' + conclusion.

claims.statement: Modeling and Alignment treat different but not independent engineering problems, resting on one shared conception of acceptable realization.
claims.contradicted_by: Collapsing the two principles into one, or denying that Alignment rests on any conception of acceptable realization — treating it as acting without one.
claims.anchor: Preface 'What the method turned out to be': the two principles solve different problems but are not independent — each rests on the same underlying conception of acceptable realization, which Modeling externalizes and Alignment enforces.

claims.statement: Building with an agent is running a printer, not a coder: suspect the instructions before the agent's capability.
claims.contradicted_by: Treating a bad output as a fixed capability ceiling by reflex, without first examining the instructions, representation, task boundary, or environment.
claims.anchor: Preface through-line + 1.1 the-printer / whose-fault-is-it: the agent is a printer; a bad output is first evidence about the instructions, representation, task boundary, or environment, not by reflex a fixed capability ceiling.

claims.statement: Host-specific resource limits live in a per-host scheduler profile, not by forking the execution graph.
distinguishes: a per-host scheduler profile — host limits set as scheduling parameters against one shared graph
forking the execution graph — a separate invariant-DAG edited per host
claims.contradicted_by: Prose that models a host's resource limits by editing or forking the execution graph itself, rather than as a per-host scheduling profile over one shared graph.
claims.anchor: The Physical View (3.5/3.6): host-specific resource limits are a per-host scheduler profile — `plan = plan_for(host_profile)` — over one shared invariant-DAG, not a forked graph per host. No chapter yet lands 'profile edit, not graph edit' as a dedicated named formulation; the profile-edit-not-graph-edit slogan's fix-wave canonicalizes it. A Modeling-Principle instance: the deployment view is a model (a scheduling profile), not an edit to the executable graph.

claims.statement: Churn's recurring causes are weak representation (knowledge rediscovered) and weak enforcement (obligations re-inspected).
